messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Hindi, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Hindi line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
मैंने ऊपर देखा और उसकी कंधे देखे वे पहले ही ग्रह की किरणों से ढके हुए थे जो हर रास्ते पर लोगों को सीधा ले जाता है।

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (Hindi translation from Step 2)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Hindi) | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------| | guardai | “I looked” (first perceptual action) | मैंने | “I (have) …” (subject + auxiliary) | OK | | in | preposition marking direction “in” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (direction expressed by “ऊपर”) | | alto | “high / upward” | ऊपर | “up / high” | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction “and” | और | “and” | OK | | vidi | “I saw” (second perceptual action) | देखे | “saw” (plural past) | OK | | le | definite article (feminine plural) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (Hindi has no article) | | sue | possessive adjective “its” (referring to the shoulders) | उसकी | “its / his” | OK | | spalle | “shoulders” (direct object) | कंधे | “shoulders” | OK | | vestite | past participle “clothed / covered” | ढके हुए थे | “were clothed / were covered” | OK | | già | adverb “already” (temporal marker) | पहले ही | “already / earlier” | OK | | de' | preposition + article “of the” (genitive) | की | “of / ’s” (genitive marker) | OK | | raggi | “rays” (source of light) | किरणों | “rays” | OK | | del | preposition + article “of the” (genitive) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (genitive already expressed by “की”) | | pianeta | “planet” (emitter of rays) | ग्रह | “planet” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “that” (introducing clause) | जो | “that / who” | OK | | mena | verb “lead / conduct” (present) | ले जाता है | “leads / conducts” | OK | | dritto | adverb “straight / aright” (manner) | सीधा | “straight / directly” | OK | | altrui | “men / people” (indirect object) | लोगों को | “people (to)” | OK | | per | preposition “along / for” (route) | पर | “on / along” | OK | | ogne | archaic “every” (quantifier) | हर | “every” | OK | | calle | “path / way” (object of preposition) | रास्ते | “paths / ways” | OK |
---
### Items that need attention
| Type | Source Word(s) | Reason | |------|----------------|--------| | **UNNECESSARY** | in, le, del | Hindi does not require these articles/prepositions; the meaning is conveyed by other words (“ऊपर”, “की”). | | **GRAMMAR** | vidi → “देखे” (plural past) vs. singular “spalle” | The Hindi verb is in plural form while “spalle” is plural, so agreement is acceptable; however, a more natural Hindi phrasing would be “उसकी कंधें देखीं”. This is a minor stylistic issue, not a hard error. | | **GRAMMAR** | “मैंने ऊपर देखा और उसकी कंधे देखे” – the second clause lacks a subject marker and the noun‑verb agreement is informal. A smoother version would be “मैंने ऊपर देखा और उसकी कंधें देखीं”. | Minor grammatical/style mismatch. |
All other source tokens are represented correctly in the Hindi translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Hindi script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Hindi text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 16** - Original: मैंने ऊपर देखा और उसकी कंधे देखे - Issue: Grammar – verb agreement and plural form of “कंधे” are incorrect. - Corrected: मैंने ऊपर देखा और उसकी कंधें देखीं
- **Line 17** - Original: वे पहले ही ग्रह की किरणों से ढके हुए थे - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- **Line 18** - Original: जो हर रास्ते पर लोगों को सीधा ले जाता है। - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
